# Session narrative -- 1000genome-workflow dftracer pipeline

run_id: `1000genome_workflow/20260725_203603`

This session ran the full dftracer pipeline (session-setup -> Pegasus/PMC
toolchain install -> dftracer install -> Python FUNCTION-mode annotation ->
baseline trace -> analyze/diagnose -> optimize across all 4 dimensions ->
validate) against `pegasus-isi/1000genome-workflow`, a pure-Python Pegasus
scientific workflow executed via `pegasus-mpi-cluster` (PMC) on Tuolumne.

Key narrative beats:

1. **Toolchain install (no compiled build system for this app):** Pegasus
   5.0.7 + Condor 10.2.2-1 (never started as daemons -- PMC-only architecture)
   + a from-source rebuild of `pegasus-mpi-cluster` against Cray MPICH, since
   the prebuilt binary was ABI-incompatible.
2. **Annotation:** 5 Python task scripts annotated with FUNCTION-mode
   `@dft_fn` decorators; one non-tool-expressible gap (module-level `tarfile`
   blocks) fixed by hand.
3. **Baseline:** a 4-node/32-rank PMC DAG run (46 tasks) measured at 316.5s,
   after an earlier `-n380` attempt hung for 16+ minutes at MPI rendezvous
   (worker over-provisioning relative to the DAG's actual max width of 17).
4. **Diagnosis:** the trace confirmed an op-count-bound (not bandwidth-bound)
   small-file fan-out in `individuals.py` -- 13.5M POSIX ops for only 73.5 GB,
   avg transfer ~5.2 KB -- plus the nuance that most of the "I/O time" was
   actually Python-level parsing overhead, not raw syscall latency.
5. **Optimization (all 4 dimensions dispatched per policy):** two composed
   app-level fixes -- `IND_ROW_PRECOMPUTE` (hoist redundant per-row VCF
   parsing, -93.4% standalone) and `IND_TAR_STREAM` (in-memory tar streaming
   instead of write-then-reread, -13.2% standalone alone but growing to
   dominate once the compute fix collapsed the parse cost) -- composed to
   -99.5%/193x at the standalone task level. Communication was found to have
   a provably zero ceiling; one compute candidate (`gc.disable`) was tested
   and rejected as a regression.
6. **Validation:** the same 4-node/32-rank DAG re-run with both optimizations
   enabled measured 244.7s vs the 316.5s baseline, a 29.3% workflow-level
   speedup -- matching the pre-registered prediction that the DAG-level delta
   would be far below the 99.5% standalone number because of a hard
   serialization barrier (`individuals_merge`) and untouched downstream tasks.
7. **Report + reproducibility validation:** this final stage assembled
   `final_report/` and ran a self-contained validation using a live Flux
   allocation. It found and fixed two real script bugs (missing venv
   activation in the smoke script; a non-self-contained dependency on an
   external wrapper script combined with PMC's rescue-file mechanism
   silently no-op'ing a "reproduction" run). The smoke test fully reproduced
   in isolation. The 4-node baseline run was confirmed to launch and execute
   real tasks correctly under the fixed scripts, but the allocation expired
   mid-DAG before completion, so the full wall-clock numbers were not
   re-measured end-to-end in this pass -- recorded honestly as
   `validated=False` rather than claimed as a pass. See `REPORT.md` Section
   12/13 for the full detail and exact resume instructions.

A mid-pipeline tool issue is also worth noting for anyone reading this file
later: two separate calls to `session_final_report` in this stage were made
without real content in the `report_md`/`readme_md`/`conversation_md`
arguments (the first omitted them entirely, the second accidentally passed a
placeholder string), which each time silently overwrote the previously
assembled detailed `REPORT.md`/`README.md`/`CONVERSATION.md` with a
near-empty default template. The content was fully reconstructed both times
from `pipeline_plan.md`, `pipeline_plan_step8_results.md`, and
`pipeline_plan_changelog.md` (which independently retained all the same
facts), and this is now flagged as a tool-gap lesson in `REPORT.md` Section
10 -- always pass the full real content for all three `_md` arguments on
every `session_final_report` call for this reason.
